summary: Same twinkle pattern with an identical per-event look (instant ignition to full value, strictly linear fade, uniform random hue) and near-perfect hue/saturation/decay dial behaviour, but the port's ignition rate is normalized per-FRAME instead of per-PIXEL, so on the default 60 px strip it fires ~4x too often at matched dials (~8x untouched) and its untouched IgnitionRate/DecaySpeed defaults differ from the original's.
observations: Rig/window: default strip, 60 px. Untouched baseline (6 s @20 fps): orig meanBrightness avg 4.3, motion avg 0.9, motionLit 14.6, zeroMotionFrames 55/120; port meanBrightness avg 39.1, motion 6.5, motionLit 13.3, zeroMotionFrames 1/120. Both brightnessTrend 'rising' (warm-up from black), both alive, no compile/runtime errors.

60 s survey @5 fps shows a single steady stochastic regime on both sides — no modes, no palette walk, no long-period beat. Late window (--skip 180, 20 s @20 fps) is statistically identical to t=0-20 s on both sides (orig 7.4% lit, port 57.3% lit), so neither side dies, saturates or drifts.

Per-event shape is IDENTICAL in kind on both sides (from 20 fps --dump traces): a pixel jumps from 0 to value 255 in one frame at full saturation, then decays strictly LINEARLY by a fixed count per frame, hue held constant for the whole event (hue drift per event: orig mean -0.000, p10/p90 -0.016/+0.017; port mean -0.005, p10/p90 -0.010/+0.010). Example orig event: 183,255,0 -> 173,240,0 -> ... -> 5,8,0 -> 0. Example port event: 0,255,75 -> 0,244,72 -> ... -> 10,7,0 -> 0.

DENSITY, default 60 px, untouched, 60 s dump of 1200 frames: orig 284 ignitions = 4.7/s = 0.079 ign/px/s, 6.9% of pixel-frames lit, mean pixel value 9.2. Port 2300 ignitions = 38.3/s = 0.639 ign/px/s, 56.3% lit, mean pixel value 84.4. That is 8.1x the ignition rate and 8.2x the lit fraction.

ROOT CAUSE — wrong normalization law. Sweeping --pixels at matched dials (orig sliderOnRate=0.5 / port sliderIgnitionRate=0.5, both sliderDecaySpeed=0.5), 20 fps: orig total ignitions/s = 3.75 (15 px), 14.05 (60), 27.9 (120), 56.7 (240), 140.6 (600) — exactly proportional to pixel count, a constant 0.234 ign/px/s (lit fraction pinned at 18.3-19.7% at every size). Port total ignitions/s = ~46 (15 px, undercounted because the strip saturates), 55.7 (60), 58.1 (120), 59.05 (240), 59.5 (600) — CONSTANT at ~59/s = ~3 ignitions per rendered frame regardless of strip length (lit fraction 97.5% / 59.5% / 36% / 20.7% / 8.6%). The two laws cross near ~240 px.

At --pixels 240 with matched dials the two waterfalls are visually indistinguishable and the statistics agree: orig 0.2363 ign/px/s, 18.9% lit vs port 0.246 ign/px/s, 20.7% lit. This is strong evidence the ONLY structural defect is the pixel-count normalization: everything downstream of picking which pixels ignite is right.

Re-ignition semantics match exactly. On the 240 px matched-dial run, ignitions landing on an already-lit pixel (resetting it to 255 with a fresh hue mid-fade): orig 217/1132 = 19.2%, port 227/1178 = 19.3%.

Frame-rate coupling is IDENTICAL on both sides and is a property of the original, not a port bug. At matched dials, ignitions/s = 7.05 / 14.05 / 28.6 (orig) and 28 / 55.7 / 112.65 (port) at 10/20/40 fps — both scale linearly with fps — while the decay step stays fixed at 15 counts/frame on BOTH sides, so full-fade time is 1.70 / 0.85 / 0.425 s on both. Lit fraction is fps-invariant on both (orig 18.3/19.1/19.6%, port 58.6/59.5/61.0%). The port/orig ignition ratio holds at 3.97 / 3.96 / 3.94 across the three rates.

IgnitionRate dial mapping has the same SHAPE but a ~4x offset at 60 px. Ignitions/s on the default rig at dial 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1: orig 4.45 / 9.90 / 14.05 / 19.0 / 28.15; port 19.65 / 38.0 / 55.7 / 72.4 / 103.8. Ratio 4.42 / 3.84 / 3.96 / 3.81 / 3.69 — a near-constant multiplier, and both curves bend upward the same way at the top of the range.

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS DIFFER. probe.json deltas of exactly 0.00 pin the original's untouched state to HueHigh=1, HueLo=0, Saturation=1, OnRate=0 (the minimum!), DecaySpeed=0.5. The port reproduces HighHue=1, LowHue=0, Saturation=1 exactly (delta 0.00) but has NO zero-delta value for either sliderIgnitionRate (min delta 47.7 at 0) or sliderDecaySpeed (min delta 8.15 at 0.5): measured untouched, its ignition rate equals its own dial ~0.25 and its fade takes 25 frames / 11 counts per frame (1.16 s) instead of the original's 18 frames / 15 counts per frame (0.85 s), i.e. a default DecaySpeed of roughly 0.35.

CONTROL-SURFACE MISMATCH: both sides expose 5 sliders, but three names/labels differ — orig sliderHueHigh(HueHigh) vs port sliderHighHue(HighHue); orig sliderHueLo(HueLo) vs port sliderLowHue(LowHue); orig sliderOnRate(OnRate) vs port sliderIgnitionRate(IgnitionRate). sliderSaturation and sliderDecaySpeed match on both name and kind. All ten controls probe responsive with value-dependence confirmed (0 vs 1 differ from each other on every one).

Colour is a match on both sides untouched: hues uniformly distributed over the whole wheel (orig hueMean 0.490, p02 0.016, p98 0.974 over 284 events; port hueMean 0.498, p02 0.020, p98 0.972 over 2300 events), saturation exactly 1.0 on every event, peak value exactly 255 on every event.

Seed-independent: at seeds 1, 7 and 1234 (untouched, 60 px, 10 s) the port sits at 38.3 / 39.1 / 38.3 ignitions/s and 55-56% lit while the original sits at 4.7 / 5.0 / 4.1 ignitions/s and 6-7% lit. The density gap is not a one-seed fluke.

dials.name: HueLo / LowHue (name differs: orig sliderHueLo, port sliderLowHue)
dials.origEffect: Lower bound of the random hue drawn per ignition. Untouched value 0. With HueLo=0.25, HueHigh=0.5 the event hues fall in [0.265, 0.497].
dials.portEffect: Identical: with LowHue=0.25, HighHue=0.5 event hues fall in [0.255, 0.492]. Same distribution, same bounds.

dials.name: HueHigh / HighHue (name differs: orig sliderHueHigh, port sliderHighHue)
dials.origEffect: Upper bound of the random hue. Untouched value 1 (full wheel). Inverted setting (HueLo=0.8 > HueHigh=0.2) degenerates to a single constant hue of exactly 0.8 for every event.
dials.portEffect: Identical, including the degenerate inverted case: LowHue=0.8, HighHue=0.2 also collapses to a constant hue of exactly 0.8. The port reproduces the original's edge-case behaviour.

dials.name: sliderSaturation
dials.origEffect: Sets HSV saturation of every event. Untouched 1.0 (fully saturated). At 0.3 every event renders at measured saturation 0.651.
dials.portEffect: At 0.3 every event renders at measured saturation 0.651 — identical value, identical name and kind.

dials.name: OnRate / IgnitionRate (name differs: orig sliderOnRate, port sliderIgnitionRate)
dials.origEffect: Sets the per-PIXEL per-frame ignition probability. 60 px @20 fps: 4.45 / 9.90 / 14.05 / 19.0 / 28.15 ignitions/s at 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1, i.e. 0.074 -> 0.469 ign/px/s. Rate per pixel is independent of strip length (0.25, 0.234, 0.233, 0.236, 0.234 ign/px/s at 15/60/120/240/600 px, dial 0.5). Untouched default = 0.
dials.portEffect: Same monotone curve shape but ~3.7-4.4x hotter on the 60 px default rig (19.65 / 38.0 / 55.7 / 72.4 / 103.8 ignitions/s), because the rate is a fixed COUNT PER FRAME (~3/frame at dial 0.5) rather than a per-pixel probability: total ignitions/s is ~59 at 60, 120, 240 and 600 px alike. Untouched default sits around its own 0.25 rather than 0.

dials.name: sliderDecaySpeed
dials.origEffect: Sets the linear fade step. Counts subtracted per frame at dial 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1: 2 / 9 / 15 / 21 / 28, i.e. full-fade times of 6.38 / 1.42 / 0.85 / 0.61 / 0.46 s at 20 fps. Untouched default = 0.5.
dials.portEffect: Dial MAPPING matches almost exactly: 2 / 8 / 15 / 21 / 27 counts per frame (6.38 / 1.59 / 0.85 / 0.61 / 0.47 s). Only the untouched DEFAULT is wrong — 11 counts/frame (1.16 s) instead of 15 (0.85 s), i.e. roughly dial 0.35.

feedback: PRIMARY FIX — ignition rate normalization. The original draws an independent per-pixel ignition each frame: total ignitions per second scale linearly with strip length (0.234 ign/px/s at dial 0.5, measured constant across 15/60/120/240/600 px). The port instead lights a fixed number of pixels per frame (~3 at dial 0.5), so its total is pinned near 59 ignitions/s at every strip length. Make the ignition decision per pixel, not a fixed budget per frame — i.e. remove whatever divides the rate by (or indexes into) pixelCount. Target on the default 60 px strip at dial 0.5: 14 ignitions/s and ~19% of pixel-frames lit; the port currently produces 56 ignitions/s and ~60% lit. Sanity check the fix at 600 px too, where the port is currently 2.4x too SPARSE (59 vs 141 ignitions/s) — the two laws happen to coincide near 240 px, so testing at one rig size can hide this.

SECONDARY — untouched default of the ignition slider. The original's untouched state is exactly its OnRate = 0 (the bottom of the slider; probe delta 0.00), giving 4.45 ignitions/s on 60 px. The port's untouched state corresponds to about its own dial 0.25. After the normalization fix, set the port's initial ignition-rate variable to the value its own slider maps to 0.

SECONDARY — untouched default of DecaySpeed. The dial MAPPING is already correct (2/8/15/21/27 vs the original's 2/9/15/21/28 counts per frame at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1), so only the initial value is wrong: the port fades at 11 counts/frame (1.16 s from 255 to 0 at 20 fps) untouched, the original at 15 counts/frame (0.85 s). Set the port's initial decay variable to what its slider produces at 0.5.

CONTROL NAMES — rename three sliders to match the original's surface, since a user's saved control values are keyed by name: sliderHighHue -> sliderHueHigh, sliderLowHue -> sliderHueLo, sliderIgnitionRate -> sliderOnRate (labels HighHue/LowHue/IgnitionRate -> HueHigh/HueLo/OnRate). sliderSaturation and sliderDecaySpeed are already correct.

DO NOT CHANGE — these were measured as exact matches and are easy to break while fixing the above: instant one-frame rise to value 255 at full saturation; strictly linear fade; hue held constant for the whole event; uniform hue draw over [HueLo, HueHigh] including the degenerate constant-hue behaviour when the bounds are inverted; saturation dial mapping (0.3 -> 0.651 on both); re-ignition of an already-lit pixel resetting it to 255 with a new hue (19.2% vs 19.3% of ignitions at matched density); and the frame-coupled timing (ignitions per second scale with fps, fade step fixed per frame) which the original also has.
